title: Practice: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids

questions.stem: When sodium is added to water, it fizzes vigorously on the surface and the solution turns alkaline. What are the products of this reaction?
questions.explanation: When reactive metals react with water, they produce a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas. The equation is: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2. The sodium hydroxide dissolves to make the solution alkaline, and the hydrogen gas causes the fizzing.

questions.stem: A student adds magnesium ribbon to dilute sulfuric acid. She observes bubbling and the magnesium dissolves. Which balanced equation represents this reaction?
questions.explanation: Metal + acid -> salt + hydrogen gas. Magnesium reacts with sulfuric acid to produce magnesium sulfate and hydrogen: Mg + H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + H2. The bubbling is hydrogen gas being produced. Magnesium is divalent (2+) and sulfate is also 2-, so the formula MgSO4 is correct.

questions.stem: A student tests four metals with dilute hydrochloric acid. Zinc reacts steadily, iron reacts slowly, copper shows no reaction, and magnesium reacts vigorously. What is the correct order of reactivity from most to least reactive?
questions.explanation: The vigour of reaction with acid indicates reactivity. Magnesium reacts most vigorously (most reactive), zinc reacts steadily, iron reacts slowly, and copper does not react (least reactive, below hydrogen in the reactivity series). Order: Mg > Zn > Fe > Cu.

questions.stem: Iron reacts with steam but not with cold water. Which products are formed when iron reacts with steam?
questions.explanation: Less reactive metals like iron react with steam (not cold water) to produce a metal oxide and hydrogen gas: 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2. This is different from very reactive metals (like sodium) that react with cold water to form hydroxides.

questions.stem: A student collects the gas produced when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid and holds a burning splint to it. What would she observe?

options.text: The gas relights a glowing splint
The gas burns with a squeaky pop
The gas has no effect on the splint

questions.explanation: The gas produced when metals react with acids is hydrogen. The test for hydrogen gas is to hold a burning splint near the gas - it burns with a squeaky pop. A glowing splint relighting is the test for oxygen, and turning limewater milky is the test for carbon dioxide.
